met_analysis:
The Depression over Southeast & adjoining Southwest Bay of Bengal moved nearly northwards with the speed of 10 kmph during past 03 hours and lies centered at 0830 hours IST of today, the 15th November, 2026 over the same region, near Latitude 9.3°N and Longitude 86.9°E, about 630 km east of Trincomalee (Sri Lanka), 690 km west-southwest of Sri Vijaya Puram (Andaman & Nicobar Islands), 840 km east-southeast of Chennai (Tamil Nadu), 1010 km south-southeast of Visakhapatnam (Andhra Pradesh) and 1130 km south-southeast of Gopalpur (Odisha). It is very likely to move north-northwestwards, intensify further into a Cyclonic Storm over the central parts of south & adjoining westcentral Bay of Bengal on 16th November and into a Severe Cyclonic Storm over westcentral Bay of Bengal on 17th November, 2026. Thereafter, it is likely to intensify further and move northwestwards towards Andhra Pradesh coast during subsequent 2 days.
The east-west trough from the cyclonic circulation associated with the above Depression over Southeast & adjoining Southwest Bay of Bengal to northern parts of Maldives and extends upto 1.5 km above mean sea level persists.
The Western Disturbance as a cyclonic circulation over north Pakistan & neighbourhood at 3.1 km above mean sea level persists with a trough aloft in middle tropospheric westerlies with its axis at 5.8 km above mean sea level now runs roughly along long 70°E to the north of Lat 32°N.
An upper air cyclonic circulation lies over Southwest Rajasthan & neighbourhoodat 0.9 km above mean sea level.
An upper air cyclonic circulation lies over Northeast Assam & neighbourhood between 1.5 & 3.1 km above mean sea level.
An upper air cyclonic circulation lies over Sub-Himalayan West Bengal & neighbourhood between 1.5 & 3.1 km above mean sea level.
An upper air cyclonic circulation lies over Southeast Arabian Sea off Kerala coast at 3.1 km above mean sea level.
The upper air cyclonic circulation over south Tamilnadu & neighbourhood at 3.1 km above mean sea level has become less marked.
The upper air cyclonic circulation over east Bangladesh & neighbourhood extending upto 1.5 km above mean sea level has become less marked.
